COMBINATORIAL ANALYSIS (p.864)
Table 24.8  Primitive Roots, Factorization of p-1
g, G denote the least positive and least negative (respectively) primitive roots of p. \epsilon denotes whether 10, -10 both or neither are primitive roots.
p  p-1  g  -G  \epsilon
3  2  2  1  -10
5  2^2  2  2  -----
7  2\cdot3  3  2  10
11  2\cdot5  2  3  -----
13  2^2\cdot3  2  2  -----
359  2\cdot179  7  2  -10
367  2\cdot3\cdot61  6  2  10
373  2^2\cdot3\cdot31  2  2  -----
821  2^2\cdot5\cdot41  2  2  \pm10
823  2\cdot3\cdot137  3  2  10
827  2\cdot7\cdot59  2  3  -10
1291  2\cdot3\cdot5\cdot43  2  4  10
1297  2^4\cdot3^4  10  10  \pm10
(Rows sampled, not exhaustive: the printed table lists primes p=3 up through 1297 across 3 side-by-side blocks; the rows above are the first 5 of block 1, the first 3 of block 2, and the first 3 plus last 2 of block 3, per the dense-table convention in data/README.md.)
note: Dense table (Table 24.8, Primitive Roots, three side-by-side blocks, ~150 primes on this page). Definitional header text kept in full; sampled rows verified: p prime and p-1 equals the printed factorization, via sympy, for every row transcribed.
